Pechera Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Pechera was the actual site of a Romanian-run concentration camp established here on December 1, 1941, which absorbed thousands of Jews deported from communities across the region — including Tulchyn and Shpykiv, both documented elsewhere in this collection — with between 6,500 and 11,000 people held there in total and an estimated 2,500 to 4,000 dying before 1,550 survivors were liberated in March 1944. This cemetery, in use since at least 1880, was already shared with the Jewish community of Shpykiv even before the war; a July 1919 pogrom had earlier killed nearly all of Pechera's own Jews, leaving just 62 by 1926.
